plotting_plan.title: Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
plotting_plan.objective: Create a scatter plot in R/ggplot2 containing exactly the three recorded pairs (b, MSE): (0, 9), (1.5, 2.25), and (3, 0). Label both axes and the recorded values. Do not add fitted curves, interpolated observations, uncertainty intervals, or extrapolated values. The caption must identify this as one deterministic calculation evaluated on the same five observations used to determine the correction. plotting_plan.title: Residual-Based Intercept Correction on Five Observations
plotting_plan.objective: Create a LaTeX/TikZ schematic showing input x and observed target y, baseline prediction 2x, residual y-2x, mean residual b=3, corrected prediction 2x+b, and evaluation on the same five observations. Use mathematical labels and explicit dependency arrows from the observed targets and baseline predictions to the residuals, and from the residuals to the correction. Make the reuse of observations for correction and evaluation visible. Include no training modules, optimizer, additional experiments, or claims of predictive generalization. Retain the editable .tex source, vector PDF, and manuscript-compatible preview as downstream reproducibility artifacts.

introduction_strategy.candidate_paper_target: Screen 10–20 macro-level contextual papers for the research graph; this is a discovery target, not a manuscript citation quota.
introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Foundational or survey literature may establish why separating systematic prediction offsets from residual error is useful for explaining prediction assessment. Verify this educational motivation without asserting real-world urgency or an application impact unsupported by the supplied materials.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: The teaching question is whether adding the mean residual removes the fixed offset of the supplied predictor on exactly x=[-2,-1,0,1,2] with y=2x+3. The supplied calculation answers only this finite, same-sample question; it establishes no literature gap, algorithmic novelty, benchmark advantage, or held-out performance.
search_directions: Search foundational or review literature for 'prediction systematic additive offset residual interpretation'; assess whether it supports the teaching motivation without importing application results.
Search 'survey regression residual analysis prediction error assessment' for broad terminology and conceptual context.
Search 'foundations fixed slope intercept least squares residual mean' to identify foundational treatments of scalar intercept estimation.
Search 'review fitted sample error versus held out prediction assessment' for broad context explaining the limits of evaluating on observations used to determine a correction.
Identify 3–5 foundational sources among the screened candidates, verifying their bibliographic records before recommending any citation.

related_work_strategy.candidate_paper_target: Screen 30–50 technical contextual candidates across the two clusters, subject to relevance. Do not pad the manuscript or retain irrelevant papers to satisfy the discovery target.
related_work_strategy.overview: Investigate two overlapping technical perspectives on the supplied arithmetic: intercept adjustment with a fixed slope, and estimation of a scalar correction from residuals. These are contextual perspectives, not newly introduced experimental competitors. The only recorded comparison is the supplied predictor with b=0, b=1.5, and b=3.

subsections.subsection_title: Research cluster: Fixed-Predictor Additive Intercept Adjustment
subsections.methodology_cluster: Scalar intercept adjustment with the predictor slope held fixed
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find technically relevant treatments available through 2026-11, including recent discussions where useful, of adjusting an additive intercept while holding the predictor fixed. Record assumptions and formulations for context. Do not seek new competitors to beat or describe any discovered method as experimentally evaluated here.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: For the supplied observations, the unadjusted predictor 2x leaves a residual of 3 at every point. This is a directly observed limitation of this particular fixed predictor, not evidence that a broader family of methods fails.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: The supplied calculation adds b=mean(y-2x)=3 to the unchanged predictor. Explain this as an elementary finite correction, with no novelty claim.

subsections.subsection_title: Research cluster: Residual-Based Scalar Correction and Evaluation
subsections.methodology_cluster: Mean-residual correction estimated and assessed on observed data
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find narrow technical sources published through 2026-11 addressing residual-derived scalar corrections and the interpretation of evaluating a correction on its estimation observations. Use these sources to explain evaluation scope, without importing additional datasets, baseline methods, or performance results.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Because the same five observations determine and evaluate b, zero corrected error describes those observations only. The supplied materials do not establish whether the correction transfers to unseen inputs or targets.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: The note makes the dependency explicit in fig_residual_workflow and reports the finite calculation transparently. It does not resolve the absence of held-out evidence or claim generalization.
